This package checks SwiftASN1 1.7.3 using its 118 shipped XCTest tests, an independent reference model and 41 runtime mutants. The main result is [15 proposed test cases + 2 deferred (depth 50 and OID 1.39)](acceptance/MISSING-TESTS.md), from 17 survivors. Each surviving mutant leaves the shipped suite green and makes its package discriminator red. The PR is made by **applying `upstream-tests.patch` to main**, pinned to `917b472dbe53ba699cbb0495f9a95a084bc6364d`. The [patch](acceptance/upstream-tests.patch) adds 12 tests, extends the ASCII-only `testUTF8StringCanCreateAString` with two non-ASCII checks, and repairs a missing rejection assertion in `testSequenceMustConsumeAllNodes`. OID 1.39 is already covered by open PR #132; mutant 21 fires only on input byte 79. The duplicate sequence test is package evidence only. Tag-based whole-file copies in `acceptance/upstream/` are excluded from publication; applying the patch preserves main's #134 tests. Complete patched release and pinned-main suites are compiled and run independently; applicability, compilation and execution are recorded separately.

[Conformance findings](acceptance/FINDINGS.md) distinguish reproduced deviations, known issues, documented restrictions and an ambiguous recommendation. BER INTEGER sign padding and CR-only PEM line endings differ from the selected rules. Known EOC handling is fixed on `main` by #134; OID decoding (#132), UTF-8 validation (#129) and opaque string validation (#130) remain unchanged. The UniversalString literal initializer stores UTF-8 bytes; this separate generation deviation has no established matching issue. Issue #110 and its fix #111 addressed the same literal-encoding bug in BMPString and provide precedent. The GeneralizedTime Double constructor has an encoder bug: it aborts at an assert in debug and serializes malformed GeneralizedTime `20260101000000.-05Z` in release for `0.00001`, on both versions. The `-05` fraction breaks the GeneralizedTime syntax and cannot be parsed back. Parsed fractional digits round trip correctly.

The original reference corpus had 153,146 requests. The revised corpus has 153,206 requests, including real SET OF and nonempty BIT STRING cases. It checks DER/BER envelopes, identifier and length boundaries, nesting, basic values, string alphabets, time syntax, PEM wrapping and base64, plus four programmatic fractional-second inputs. It exhausts byte inputs of length zero, one and two and uses seed `6902021` for longer generated inputs. It tests truncation at every position in the generated envelopes. Serializer checks include DER framing fidelity, typed round trips and SET OF ordering. There is no streaming API, so prefix checks do not claim incremental parsing support.

The X.690 PDF was unavailable. Every X.690 clause row has `source = "secondary"`, using the subject's comments, the supplied RFC 5280 and the cited clause structure. The three supplied RFC texts are primary sources. This limits the strength and completeness of the normative comparison. CER and certificate-specific GeneralizedTime policy are declared inapplicable to this generic module.

The [whole public API acceptance file](acceptance/acceptance.toml) lists compiler-extracted public symbols, inherited and synthesized members, conformance edges and source declarations omitted from the graph. [PUBLIC-API.md](acceptance/PUBLIC-API.md) is the readable inventory. Items without an isolated semantic assertion are explicit gaps. The 41 weighted behaviour claims each have an observed-red runtime control; public visibility alone supplies no weight. The separate [conformance projection](acceptance/conformance.toml) has one row per selected external clause. Its partial rows claim only their tested sub-rule. Each reference evidence row derives its result and case count from requests attributed to that clause; clause rows and their uncontrolled comparison evidence stay unweighted. Only the separate mutation-backed behaviour rows carry weight. Passing time or base64 evidence is never relabelled as a failure elsewhere. Validator success means that these records are well formed, not that every public item or applicable clause is proved.

Re-run offline with Swift 6.4, its macOS SDK, Python 3.14 and local Git mirrors containing the pinned commits. The runner derives the native target triple with `swift -print-target-info`. Builds, caches and disposable validation trees stay in this folder. SwiftASN1 has no external package dependencies.

Prepare the subject and validator checkouts from local mirrors before running. Existing supplied published trees need no preparation. The subject Git checkout must contain both commits; a source-only export is insufficient. The runner pins main by commit and does not follow a branch reference.

```sh
export ASN1_MIRROR=/path/to/local/swift-asn1-mirror
export FORMAT_MIRROR=/path/to/local/acceptance-format-mirror
mkdir -p published/swift-asn1-1.7.3
git clone --no-hardlinks "$ASN1_MIRROR" published/swift-asn1-git
git -C published/swift-asn1-git checkout --detach 3b6410f7dee09eb33cdd26260c5fd47fda19b0e2
git -C published/swift-asn1-git cat-file -e 917b472dbe53ba699cbb0495f9a95a084bc6364d^{commit}
git -C published/swift-asn1-git archive 3b6410f7dee09eb33cdd26260c5fd47fda19b0e2 | tar -x -C published/swift-asn1-1.7.3
git clone --no-hardlinks "$FORMAT_MIRROR" acceptance-format
export ACCEPTANCE_FORMAT="$PWD/acceptance-format"
git -C "$ACCEPTANCE_FORMAT" checkout --detach e471a3c689cd1fec9d751a09972d1d785fb56765
```

The validator source is [ivmat/acceptance-format](https://github.com/ivmat/acceptance-format), pinned to `e471a3c689cd1fec9d751a09972d1d785fb56765`. Preparation and execution use local files; no network is needed. The included `published/SHA256SUMS.txt` verifies the exact tag export. Avoid overwriting a prepared published tree.

With checkouts prepared:

```sh
export ACCEPTANCE_FORMAT=/path/to/acceptance-format
./run_all.sh
```

The script uses seven build invocations: three debug harnesses, two release harnesses for D4, and two complete patched repository suites. Only one build contains mutation schemata. All mutation runs use `swift test --skip-build`; `ASN1_MUTANT` is read once through a `static let`. No mutant needs its own build. Expected-red specification tests are checked as failures, including isolated debug process termination. D4 asserts exact serialization and a round trip and also fails in release. Parsed-value round trips pass in both modes. Build counts, elapsed times, exact results and hashes appear under [acceptance/evidence/gen](acceptance/evidence/gen). Published checksums and the git checkout's clean state are verified before and after the run.

The script runs `check_acceptance.py --strict`, the conformance checker and evidence consistency checks. Both format validators pass. Their remaining warnings concern experimental coverage denominators and legacy A1 warning text; those warnings are not proof of full API coverage. [SWIFT-NOTES.md](acceptance/SWIFT-NOTES.md) records the language adaptations and preparation build attempts.

Limits include the explicit API gaps, finite input lengths, the parser's depth limit, secondary X.690 citations, opaque Teletex semantics, unsupported BER forms, generic protocol implementers and concurrency laws. No unbounded crash or hang guarantee is claimed. The local issue and PR snapshots and main commit are pinned in the evidence; no online completeness claim is made.

## Notes

D3 is an API-hardening note. The caller supplies the PEM label, the generator copies it verbatim, and the parser round-trips its own output. An invalid caller label can produce text outside the RFC 7468 grammar. The observation and repro remain in the Notes section of [FINDINGS.md](acceptance/FINDINGS.md); D3 is excluded from the issue list. The issue candidates are D1, D2, D4 and D5.
